<reason>A won a competitive debate by keeping the actual motion in view: product-liability-style duties misfit general-purpose models, while existing negligence already covers documented ignored risks. B was punchier on victims, joint causation, and “who pays,” but repeatedly collapsed the clash into whether a reckless maker should ever pay—a claim A never denied. A answered the immunity fork honestly, kept cheapest-avoider/control and hindsight problems live, and showed comparative fault cannot define a defect in unguarded language.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2 (A4.3–A4.6) rejecting B’s immunity/concession fork: liability for a documented ignored risk is negligence, not product-liability for model behavior, and B cannot both discharge duty via warnings and treat unguarded language as the product.</best_rebuttal>
